how_it_behaves: Login opens a calendar behind a central OpenEMR Product Registration modal and sometimes a browser Save password panel, both of which block work. The top demographics search and the Patient Finder table filter are unreliable: they can show no matches, lose results on refresh, and return look-alike patients. The reliable route is Patient > Search or Add Patient, entering first and last name, using the grey Search button at the bottom (never Create New Patient), then picking the exact name row in the results popup. Typing into the First Name and Last Name search boxes can be read back incorrectly by a single-screenshot reader even when the boxes visibly contain the full correctly typed names, for example dropping or altering a final letter; those two type steps therefore must not rely on the type step's own read-back, and the typed names are instead verified by requiring the exact '{last}, {first}' row to be visible in the search results popup before that row is clicked. The search results popup can be a long alphabetically ordered list containing many patients, so the exact matching row may be far down the list and not reached after only a couple of scrolls; it must be sought by repeatedly scrolling the popup list a little at a time and re-checking for the exact row after each scroll, continuing well beyond the first few scrolls, rather than assuming the row is absent if it is not seen early in the list. A chart's plain-text heading after 'Medical Record Dashboard -' gives the patient name; the blue header above it has look-alike ID and DOB values. Verify that heading with a yes/no ensure only: reading the heading name as a field can return nothing even when the heading is plainly showing, so a read-and-compare of it must not be used to confirm the patient. Demographics in the Dashboard Who panel holds External ID (the plan member ID) and DOB. On the Issues page, Medical Problems and Medications are separate sections; each row has a '>' expander at its far left that opens inline dates and comments and pushes later rows down, so rows must be re-found by title before expanding. Expanding a row near the bottom of the screen turns its '>' into a down chevron but puts the expanded detail below the visible area, so after expanding a row you must scroll down to bring that detail into view before checking for or reading it. Expanding a row higher up the screen may already show its detail with no scrolling at all, and a fixed or large scroll after expanding can push that row itself off the top of the screen while its detail remains below; so after expanding, first check whether the detail is already visible and only scroll in small one-notch steps while it is not, and do not require the title row and its detail table to be on screen at the same time, since bringing lower detail into view can move the title just out of view. The expanded detail under a row is not separate date/comment lines: it is a small table with column headings such as 'Last Modified', 'Start Date', 'End Date' and 'Comments' on one line and the values on the line underneath those headings; a row with no start or end date may omit those two columns entirely, showing only 'Last Modified' and 'Comments'. Such a row is a complete, valid row: its 'Comments' value is still present and must be read, and the row must still be recorded with its dates simply absent, not skipped, dropped, or read as entirely empty because the date columns are missing. A medication title and its expanded detail table can be split across two views by a large scroll, and a list read then records the title with empty detail, so list reads over the expanded Medications section must scroll in small steps so each title stays on screen together with its detail table. A diagnosis code sits in parentheses at the very end of a Medical Problems blue title, just before a separate parenthesised status word such as (Active); the code and the status are two different parenthesised parts and must be read as separate fields. The Issues page is shown in a 'Patient Issues' tab alongside Calendar, Message Center and Visit History tabs, with no Dashboard link visible in that tab row or elsewhere on that page, so identity cannot be re-read by clicking a Dashboard link after going to Issues; read identity from the Dashboard before opening Issues and do not navigate back afterwards. This job is read-only.

skills.name: read_patient_chart
skills.does: Log in, open the named patient's chart, and read their plan member ID, date of birth, diagnosis code and medication history without changing anything. Identity is read once, from the Dashboard before going to Issues, because the Issues page offers no Dashboard link to return with, so there is deliberately no second identity read at the end.
